question.prompt:
When a positive integer \(N\) is fed into a machine, the output is a number calculated according to the rule shown below.

[Figure 1](figures/2020_AMC_8_Q22_question_fig1.svg)

For example, starting with an input of \(N=7,\) the machine will output \(3 \cdot 7 + 1 = 22.\) Then if the output is repeatedly inserted into the machine five more times, the final output is \(26.\) \[ \begin{align*} &7 \to 22 \to 11 \to 34 \\ &\to 17 \to 52 \to 26 \end{align*} \] When the same \(6\)-step process is applied to a different starting value of \(N,\) the final output is \(1.\) What is the sum of all such integers \(N?\) \[ \begin{align*} &N \to \underline{\phantom{00}} \to \underline{\phantom{00}} \to \underline{\phantom{00}}\\ &\to \underline{\phantom{00}} \to \underline{\phantom{00}} \to 1 \end{align*} \]

solutions.explanation:
Work backward from the required final output \(1\), because each backward step has at most two possibilities.

An output \(m\) can come from the even input \(2m\). It can also come from \((m-1)/3\), but only when that is a positive odd integer, since the rule \(3N+1\) applies only to odd inputs. For example, \(4\) can come from \(8\) or \(1\), whereas \(8\) can come only from \(16\).

Applying those rules gives the following complete sets:

\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
\text{Steps backward}&\text{Possible values}\\\hline
0&1\\
1&2\\
2&4\\
3&1,\ 8\\
4&2,\ 16\\
5&4,\ 5,\ 32\\
6&1,\ 8,\ 10,\ 64
\end{array}
\]

Thus the starting values are \(1,8,10,64\), whose sum is \(1+8+10+64=\boxed{83}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\). The value \(1\) is allowed: its cycle \(1\to4\to2\to1\) returns to \(1\) after six steps as well.
solutions.title: Reverse each machine step, checking the predecessor's parity
